description: Read one incident in full, with every alert sent for it. It has id, monitor_id or heartbeat_id (exactly one is set), monitor (id, name and type) or heartbeat (id and name), started_at, created_at, resolved_at, cause, cause_detail, last_notified_at, acknowledged_at, acknowledged_by, acknowledged_via, acknowledged_by_label, acknowledged_by_user, renotify_count (how many reminders listed this incident) and notification_logs (each alert attempt: id, channel_type, destination, channel_label (the channel's label when the alert was sent; null for a channel without a label, a member's own email, a fallback email or an alert older than the field), event TRIGGERED (the first alert only; reminders are not logged here) or RESOLVED, sent_at, status PENDING, SENT or FAILED, and error; SSL alerts (SSL_EXPIRY, SSL_RENEWAL_OVERDUE, SSL_COVERAGE_LOST), change alerts (CHANGE_DETECTED) and domain alerts (DOMAIN_EXPIRY, DOMAIN_ON_HOLD, DOMAIN_NOT_IN_REGISTRY) are not tied to an incident and never appear here). started_at is the outage start: the first failing check of the streak (for a heartbeat, the missed deadline, or when the /fail ping arrived). created_at is when the incident was confirmed and its first alert went out, often minutes after started_at. resolved_at is when it ended: the check that confirmed recovery, or the pause, deletion or plan downgrade that closed it (null while open). acknowledged_at is when someone acknowledged it (null if nobody has). An incident's duration is resolved_at minus started_at. Use it to tell whether its alerts were delivered and who acknowledged it: acknowledged_by is the Fettle user's uuid (null for a Telegram tap), acknowledged_by_user that user's id and name (null for a Telegram tap, an acknowledgement recorded before the source was stored or a deleted user), acknowledged_via the source (DASHBOARD, API_KEY, MCP or TELEGRAM; null when unacknowledged or acknowledged before the source was recorded) and acknowledged_by_label the actor that is not a Fettle user (the Telegram name, the API key name or the MCP client name). MCP means acknowledged through the remote Fettle MCP endpoint (label: the connected app's name, or the API key's name when that connection uses a key); the stdio fettle-mcp package and any REST call with an API key record API_KEY (label: the key's name). For the person's email use get_incident_context. destination is an email address, a Telegram chat id, or only scheme://host/… of a webhook. To find incidents use list_incidents; to stop its reminders use acknowledge_incident.

incident_id.description: The incident's uuid from list_incidents. An id that is not an incident of this organization is a 404.

name: get_incident

acknowledged_at.description: When someone acknowledged the incident; null if nobody has.

name.description: The user's current first and last name.

acknowledged_by_user.description: The Fettle user behind acknowledged_by; null while unacknowledged, for a Telegram tap, for an acknowledgement recorded before the source was stored and for a user deleted since.

anyOf.description: Known values: DASHBOARD, API_KEY, MCP, TELEGRAM.

cause.description: Known values: TIMEOUT, DNS_FAILURE, CONNECTION_REFUSED, TLS_INVALID, HTTP_4XX, HTTP_5XX, HTTP_UNEXPECTED_STATUS, KEYWORD_MISSING, TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS, TARGET_BLOCKED, PORT_STATE_MISMATCH, INVALID_TARGET, HEARTBEAT_MISSED, HEARTBEAT_FAILED, UNKNOWN.

created_at.description: When the incident was confirmed (after the monitor's confirmation rounds) and its first alert went out; at or after started_at, usually by seconds to minutes.

heartbeat.description: The heartbeat that failed; null for a monitor.

last_notified_at.description: When the Down alert went out; null until it has been sent. On incidents opened before reminder digests it can be the last repeat alert instead.

type.description: Known values: HTTP, PING, SSL, TCP, DNS.

monitor.description: The monitor that failed; null for a heartbeat.

channel_label.description: The channel's label when the alert was sent. A later rename or delete of the channel does not change it. Null for a channel without a label, for a member's own email channel, for a fallback email, and on rows sent before labels were recorded.

channel_type.description: Known values: EMAIL, TELEGRAM, WEBHOOK, SLACK, DISCORD.

event.description: Known values: TRIGGERED, RESOLVED, SSL_EXPIRY, SSL_RENEWAL_OVERDUE, SSL_COVERAGE_LOST, CHANGE_DETECTED, DOMAIN_EXPIRY, DOMAIN_ON_HOLD, DOMAIN_NOT_IN_REGISTRY, REMINDER.

renotify_count.description: How many reminders listed this incident.

resolved_at.description: When the incident ended: the check that confirmed recovery (for a heartbeat, the ping that brought it back), or the pause, deletion or plan downgrade that closed it; null while the incident is open.

started_at.description: When the outage started: the first failing check of the streak, at or before created_at. For a heartbeat, the missed deadline (last ping plus period and grace), or when the /fail ping arrived. Duration and downtime count from here.

title: Get an incident
